t: NEW FIGHTER SCREEN: TRAINING, BATTLE, WIFI AND A MAP SCREEN
n: BATTLES now opens three big cards: TRAINING, BATTLE and WIFI. WIFI is the old WI-FI ROOMS card, so the mode screen now has CHALLENGES, BATTLES and STORY MODE.

The fighter screen is new and works like Mortal Kombat and Dragon Ball FighterZ: 3 faces on top (GOJO, YUJI, RYU) and 4 below (VERITY, CAT, FREDDY, SUKUNA). Tap a face to put the cursor on it: that face comes alive and the fighter shows big on the side in his idle animation, on a stage in his own colour, with his name, a tag and three of his moves. Tap the same face again or press SELECT to choose him. RANDOM runs the cursor over the fighters you may pick and lands on one (SELECT then chooses him). You choose on the left (red frame), then the enemy on the right (blue frame).

TRAINING: you, then the enemy (Gojo, Yuji, Verity or the Cat), then the map. Every fighter, Gojo too, now starts in a normal training room against the enemy you chose (SETTINGS > TRAIN > ENEMY IS follows your choice). The old free play in the street with the bystanders (Gojo, no enemy) is the yellow FREE PLAY IN THE CITY button, shown when Gojo is your fighter.

BATTLE: the old Versus mode on the same screen: you, then the enemy, with the six grades in a row under the faces (a grade you have not unlocked stays greyed), then the map, START and a VS splash before the fight (a tap skips it). Sukuna and Ryu are greyed (TRAIN ONLY) and Freddy cannot be the enemy yet; fighters you have not bought stay locked.
MAP SCREEN: two big pictures, the street and the skyscraper (taken from the game's own art), with your two fighters standing in them. A tap picks the map, START begins. The old MAP buttons are gone.

The Wi-Fi room's fighter screen has the same look (faces, your fighter on the left, the opponent on the right once you both chose, RANDOM). Only Gojo, Yuji, Verity, the Cat and Freddy can be chosen online. The network code is the old one.
The back button (and Esc) steps back: VS splash, map screen, enemy, your fighter, the three cards, the mode screen. Your last picks are remembered.

Every M1 punch or kick that would deal MORE THAN 15 damage now deals exactly 8, for every fighter, yours and the enemy's: Gojo (the elbow, the kick, the walking combo and the red mode's blows), Yuji (the downslam, the spin punch, the hooks when cursed energy is on), Verity (the last M1 punch used to hit for 35, plus 25 more as a combo finisher), Freddy Krueger (his slashes when the extras add up), the Cartoon Cat, Sukuna (his face kick, 16 before) and Ryu (his jump punch 18, downslam 17 and hard punch 16 before).

The rule looks at the final hit, after every bonus: the random extra, the combo finisher, cursed energy, the counter, the heavy swing, OPEN, FLOW and the enemy's grade. A hit of 15 or less is left as it is. The specials are not touched: BLUE and MODE moves, the Black Flash, DIVERGENT FIST, the pierce, the bite, the counters, the FATALITY, the DOMAINS and the ULTIMATES, and the curses' own blows.
Side effect to know about: with cursed energy on (x1.3 damage) most M1 hits go over 15 and become 8, so they are weaker than without it. Tell me if you want the cap to work another way.

Chapter 5 goes on after the black. Yuji opens his eyes (the lids open a little, shut, then open wide) and lies in a glass cell in Stark Tower with Iron Man standing outside, watching. "WHERE AM I?" - "THIS IS STARK TOWER." Yuji gets up and punches the glass: nothing happens (a ring runs over the glass and it rings).

TONY STARK walks in without his suit: the Iron Man that Yuji has been talking to was only the suit (it powers down when Tony arrives). "HEY." - "SO HOW DID YOU COME HERE?" Yuji starts to answer, then STEVE ROGERS walks in (blond, in a jacket): "WHO IS THIS?" - "SOMEONE FROM A DIFFERENT UNIVERSE." Tony opens the chamber, Yuji walks out, and Tony steps into the suit (a scanner runs up him as the armour closes round him): "FOLLOW ME."

Then the HUGE room: a wide shot of a hall that makes the two of them tiny, and the camera comes in. "DO YOU HAVE A PHOBIA OF LARGE PLACES?" - "NO." Tony charges and the ring closes on Yuji like before: TAP anywhere on the screen, or press any key. A good tap: Yuji ducks under the punch and everything goes into SLOW MOTION: Tony's arm, back and one leg dead straight, the other knee bent, looking down at Yuji. A miss: the punch throws Yuji across the room into the wall and he lies there hurt (the blood follows GRAPHIC DAMAGE; with it OFF the blow is cut away).

END OF CHAPTER 5 and TO BE CONTINUED now come after this part. SKIP goes road -> black, lab -> huge room (the tap counts as made), huge room -> the cards. Still no music (the song is coming): new sounds for the panel, the door and the suit.

Chapter 5 is here: THE IRON MAN. It opens in the chapter list when you finish chapter 4 (CONTINUE takes you there too) and starts right where chapter 4 stopped: Yuji and Iron Man on the freeway in New York, the blade at Yuji's chest. There is no music yet (a song is coming): the wind, the hits, the boots' thrusters and the repulser carry it.

Yuji says "AND IF I DON'T?" and Iron Man answers "WELL... THEN I WILL HAVE TO END YOU." Yuji gets into his stance, Iron Man rushes in with the blade and a ring closes on Yuji, just like in chapter 3: TAP anywhere on the screen, or press any key, as the ring reaches the middle circle. Miss it and the blade goes through Yuji's chest: black, YUJI DIED, and chapter 5 starts again from the beginning (the blood follows GRAPHIC DAMAGE: with it OFF the stab is cut away).

Hit it and Yuji dodges, punches Iron Man in the face and slides back: "WHO ARE YOU?" "I AM TONY STARK." The being with a gauntlet that had 2 stones, a laugh, "WELL THEN, COME WITH ME.", "NO!", "OH WELL." and a punch that makes Yuji bleed a little. Yuji charges with a punch, ducks a right hook and kicks Iron Man under the chin (he tanks it), dodges three blade swings at his head and takes a repulser blast to the chest. Iron Man flies after him, grabs his neck and punches him out: the screen goes dark. END OF CHAPTER 5, TO BE CONTINUED.
The SKIP button works in chapter 5 (it counts the tap as made). The chapter list now has five chapters.

t: ONE ELEVATOR, A TIGHT CAB AND NO MORE FADES
n: No more fade to black in the skyscraper. When you fall through a hole the camera FOLLOWS YOU DOWN through the floors (it speeds up like a real fall) and you land with a thud; the stairs and a launch through a broken ceiling slide up or down the same way, and the enemy stays in sight on the floor you leave. When you slam the enemy through the floor you SEE him drop through the hole, and when he flies up through a broken ceiling you see that too. Stepping into or out of the elevator is a straight cut.
The elevator cab is much more cramped: 100 pixels wide, a steel box with a mirror, a small window onto the city, a handrail and the doors in the middle of the back wall.

There is ONE elevator for the whole building. If the cab is at your floor, JUMP or CROUCH at its door gets you in. If it is somewhere else, the same press CALLS it: the number over the door counts, the doors open and wait for you about 6 seconds. If the enemy is riding it, it is IN USE: you can neither call it nor get in (the number over the door turns red).

A floor button now makes the cab wait 0.6 seconds, then the doors shut and it goes. When it arrives the doors open and wait: stand on the doors and press JUMP to get out (nothing happens by itself any more). THE TRICK: press a floor and step out in less than 0.6 seconds: the cab leaves WITHOUT you. If the enemy is inside it, he is carried to the floor you picked, alone, and has to ride back.

The enemy uses the elevator too: when he is on another floor and nobody is using the cab, he calls it to his floor, rides to yours and steps out of its door. If a door on the way is broken he takes the stairs.

Broken doors stay broken for good. When the enemy breaks into the cab (after about 8 seconds of banging) its doors are broken for the rest of the match: they never shut again and he just walks in whenever he gets there. OUT OF ORDER and torn-out floor doors stay as they are too.

t: RIDE THE ELEVATOR: A PANEL WITH ALL THE FLOORS
n: Stand at an elevator door in the skyscraper and press JUMP or CROUCH: the doors shut behind you and you are INSIDE the elevator, a steel cab with a mirror, a handrail and a window onto the city. A panel with a button for each of the 50 floors opens at the side (scroll it with your finger or the mouse wheel). The old quick ride (up or down 5 floors) is gone: the panel replaces it. Stairs work as before.

Tap a floor and the ride starts at once: the display counts the floors, the cab shakes, and a ding and the doors opening tell you that you are there. A ride takes 0.1 second a floor (1 second at least, 4 seconds at most). Through the window the city and the sky change with the height (sunset, night, clouds, rain, a storm). Above the grid are TOP, LOBBY, ENEMY'S FLOOR and LAST FLOOR. The buttons show the kind of floor, floors you have visited are lit, a red dot marks the floor of the enemy and a mark shows floors with damage.

OPEN steps you back out, CLOSE shuts the doors faster and the red STOP button halts the cab between floors until you press a floor again. Time never stops: inside the cab you can walk, jump, block and attack.

The enemy is left outside the doors. If he was on your floor he runs to them and BANGS on them, and after about 8 seconds he BREAKS IN: the fight goes on inside the cab (also during the ride, and he steps out with you). If he was on another floor he follows later, as before, and when he comes out of a door of your floor that door swings open.

Elevators can break. A couple of hard hits jam a door (OUT OF ORDER: its button on the panel is dead, and a floor with no working elevator cannot be picked). A lot of damage or a blast tears the doors out and the SHAFT is open: whoever walks into it falls all the way down to the lobby (3% of health a floor, at most 30%, never a K.O.).

t: THE SKYSCRAPER, REBUILT TO LOOK TOP NOTCH
n: The whole look of the skyscraper map is new: every floor is a hand-shaded pixel-art room with real lighting. Wood-panelled lounges with sofas and paintings, a marble lobby with a gold TOWER sign, white-tiled pantries, cold steel server rooms with blinking racks and hazard stripes, brick storage rooms with shelves and pipes, conference rooms with screens and curtains, and a penthouse with panorama windows.

The city outside changes with the height: a sunset over the rooftops on the low floors, a starry night with the moon on the high ones and a sea of clouds above everything. Every 6 floors has its own weather: clear, cloudy, rain running on the glass, fog, or a storm with lightning that lights the room.

LIGHTING: the ceiling lights, lamps, screens and vending machines light the room and the rest is darker. A blast, a slam, a wall coming down or a very hard blow shakes the lights out (glass and sparks); a floor with broken lights stays dark and its doors flash red emergency lights. A blast lights the room for a moment and leaves dust in the air.

Doors move: the stairs door swings open on the steps and the elevator doors slide apart on a lit cab, with EXIT signs and a floor display. Damage looks real: cracks grow across a wall before it goes, a broken wall leaves stumps with bent rebar and rubble, craters show broken concrete with the glow of the room below, a hole in the ceiling has a sparking cable, glass leaves shards in the frame, and blasts leave scorch marks.

4 new pieces of furniture: sofa, bookshelf, filing cabinet and water cooler (it spills a puddle). Screens, server lights, vending machines and the elevator display are animated, and glossy floors show reflections.

SETTINGS > GRAPHICS decides how much of it is on: BACKGROUND DETAIL (FLAT = no lights or weather, FULL = everything), GLOW (a warmer light) and the low-quality switch. At FULL the whole picture costs well under a millisecond a frame.

A new map: the inside of a 50-floor skyscraper. Press the MAP button on the fighter screen (free play) or the versus screen to switch between STREET and SKYSCRAPER; the choice is kept. You start on floor 50, the penthouse. The screen shows one floor at a time and its number at the top.

Every floor is made at random the first time you see it: 2 to 4 rooms in a long corridor, its own colours, furniture, lights and windows. The view outside changes with the height: a night sky with stars and the moon high up, clouds in the middle, the skyline of the neighbouring buildings low down.

SLAMS BREAK THE FLOOR. A slam (a hit that puts a fighter on the floor from above, like Ryu's DOWNSLAM or DIVE PUNCH) or a very heavy hit breaks the floor under him: 1 floor, or more the harder the hit was. He falls through the crater. A fall costs 3% of health per floor, at most 30%, and never knocks anybody out. The crater stays and anybody who walks into it falls too (or you can leave it alone). A high launch (a kick that throws him up) breaks the CEILING and sends him up a floor.

Stairs (1 floor) and elevators (5 floors) are in the rooms: stand at the door and press JUMP to go up or CROUCH to go down. The fighter who is on another floor is away and comes after you: out of the crater if you fell, by the stairs or the elevator if not. The enemy keeps away from the edge of a crater unless he is thrown in.

EVERYTHING BREAKS. Desks, chairs, tables, computers, lamps, glass, vending machines (they drop a soda that heals 6%), safes, pillars, server racks, crates and plants break when a blow lands near them, when a body is thrown into them (the heavy ones hurt) or when you attack them. Gas tanks and fire extinguishers EXPLODE: a blast that hurts both fighters, breaks what is near, can open the floor and sets off the next one. The walls between the rooms are solid until a hard throw breaks them; the glass at the ends of the floor breaks too and a fighter thrown out falls to the street (the other one drops down after him).
Everything that is broken stays broken for the whole match, even in the next round. Ryu's ULTIMATE breaks the furniture and walls in its way and its last burst breaks 3 floors under the enemy.

Ryu has an ULTIMATE now: JUST THIS ONCE. It is on the ULTIMATE button (the DOMAIN button, key V), costs 67 percent of his energy and needs 30 seconds to come back. He stands still with his feet planted and his finger held out in front of him like a gun, his hair stands out forward like a cannon and fills with light, a ball of energy gathers at its tip and the camera moves in on him while he says "JUST THIS ONCE".
Then the screen goes black and says 今回だけ, the Japanese for "just this once", and it cuts back to a huge beam that leaves his hair and crosses the whole screen.

Nothing can stop the beam: not a block, a dash, a jump or lying on the floor. It cuts the enemy for 45 percent of his health in ten hits and throws him back. The one thing that saves an enemy is to be BEHIND Ryu when it fires: then it misses him.

Nothing touches Ryu while it lasts and he cannot move; a press on any button before the beam skips straight to the beam. New sprites: 60 new pictures of him in the stance (raise the hand, charge, fire, lower it).

t: RYU: 0.2 S MORE IN THE AIR
n: Ryu stays in the air 0.2 seconds longer when he jumps (the push-off and the landing are the same, the flight is longer, so his air moves have more time: the DIVE PUNCH in his normal mode, and the AIR BLAST and the TRIPLE BLAST in the Granite Blast mode).

An enemy that Ryu launches (the KICK UP, the uppercut, the blast that pops him up and the one that throws him up) stays in the air 0.2 seconds longer too. He goes just as high, he only comes down slower.

The 0.2 seconds are real seconds: the GAME PACE setting makes the game clock run faster than the real one, so the game adds 0.25 s of its own time on FAST and 0.3 s on TURBO. The other fighters are not changed.
Ryu has a MODE button now (key E). It switches the GRANITE BLAST mode on and off. While it is on, a ring of cyan sparks rises from his hair and the button is lit.

In the mode every ATTACK is a blast out of his hair. He drives his head forward like a bull and the front of his hair turns to energy (the pictures are new: a charge, the snap of the head, the recoil). BLAST 1 and BLAST 2 come one after the other (9 and 11 damage), crouched you fire a LOW BLAST along the floor, in the air an AIR BLAST angled down at the enemy. Each costs 4% of your energy.

The beam is white in the middle, cyan round that (the beam itself) and has a very light blue outline. It reaches across the whole screen, it hits an enemy anywhere in front of you at the height of the beam, and a crouching enemy ducks under the high ones.

BLUE is GRANITE BLAST in the mode (it says so on the button): standing it is one blast that is more concentrated, so thinner and greyer, and it does 20 damage, more than the attack blasts (10% energy, 1.2 s wait). Holding back it is the DOUBLE BLAST: two blasts one after the other (12 + 13, 18% energy). In the air it is the TRIPLE BLAST: two blasts from the air (the first pops the enemy up a little), then Ryu tips his head back and looks up and the third one goes up through the enemy and throws him high (10 + 10 + 16, 30% energy).
Without the mode he is the same as before. The blasts are blocked like any blow, and nothing starts when you have too little energy.
Fixed on the way: a shot never touched an enemy who was in the air (his height is a fraction of a row and no row of his body was found). Sukuna's flying slashes hit enemies in the air now.

SETTINGS > ERRORS has a new part on top: SCAN THE GAME. It takes about a minute. The game plays itself with the sound off, on a fast clock of its own, and looks for errors in: every screen, all 7 fighters (free play and versus, with all three GRAPHIC DAMAGE settings), every button in every direction for every fighter, every FATALITY and DOMAIN played to the end, every story scene shot by shot (through the SKIP button), and the game's own tables (skills, settings, update log, sounds, page elements). A bar shows the minute, CANCEL (or the back button) stops it.

Your saves are safe: they are copied first and put back afterwards, even if the game is closed in the middle of a scan. At the end the page restarts and shows the result on the ERRORS page: how many checks passed, the errors and notes it found and where, and COPY SCAN REPORT to send it to me.

It finds errors thrown by the code, numbers that are not numbers, effect lists that only grow, cutscenes that do not start or never end, SKIP buttons that do nothing, text that does not fit your screen, and mistakes in the tables (for example a skill that has no place in the tree, which is what crashed the SUKUNA page in V1.166). It cannot see if something just looks wrong, and it cannot prove that there is no bug.

How it was tested: 10 faults were put into the game on purpose (a skill with no place, a skill that needs a skill that does not exist, an error in a hit, a broken number, a list that grows, a FATALITY that does not start, a broken SKIP button, a screen that crashes, an error in a timer, a missing update log entry) and the scan found all 10. On the game as it is, it found nothing in 120000 frames. The more time is left of the minute, the more extra random fights it plays.
Also: the back button of the phone stops a running scan.

Every story cutscene has a SKIP button in the top right corner now, like chapter 4: it goes on to the next shot. Tapping anywhere on a cutscene still does the same. It is in chapter 1 (the alley), part 2 (the hall, the training, the Master, the report), chapter 2 and chapter 3. Chapter 4 keeps its own. In chapter 3 it hides while the how-to-play card or the defeat card is on the screen, because tapping does something else there.

SETTINGS (from the main menu) has a new ERRORS page. The game writes down every error it runs into (and keeps going), newest first, with the time and where it happened. COPY REPORT copies the version, the window size, your settings and the errors, so you can send it to me. CLEAR empties the list. The page button shows how many errors there are. The last 30 are kept, even after you close the game.
The NEW MISSION message of chapter 1 moved down a little so the SKIP button does not touch it.
Not included: the cutscenes inside fights (the FATALITIES, domains and finishers) have no SKIP button yet. Sukuna's finisher has its own skip.
SKILLS > SUKUNA opened with an error since the last update: the new FATALITY skill had no place in the tree. It sits at the bottom of Sukuna's tree now, and it needs the AIR CUT like before.

The people walking in the street carry their things properly: the businessman's briefcase, the woman's bag and the old man's cane (a double name in the code made the carry pose never apply, so their arms hung wrong).
Chapter 1: the title card (CHAPTER 1, THE MYSTERY) lay on top of the NEW MISSION message. It is lower now, so the two never touch.

The fighter select shows seven fighters but was sized for six. On a 16:9 screen (most computers and some tablets) and on small phones (640 x 360) GOJO and RYU were cut off at the edges. All seven fit now.
SETTINGS > GAME on a short screen: the title and the CLOSE button went off the edge. The page scrolls inside now, and the title and CLOSE always stay on the screen.
DOMAIN fits its button on small screens (on a 360 pixel high screen the letters were cut at the sides).
On a computer the Esc key leaves a story scene, like the Android back button does. Before, there was no way out of a cutscene with the keyboard.

How it was checked: every fighter played at random (free play and versus, all three GRAPHIC DAMAGE settings), every button of every screen clicked at random, chapters 1 to 4 played at random, and every screen looked at in ten window sizes. Nothing else came up. I cannot promise that no bug is left, so if you see one, tell me.

Sukuna has a FATALITY now: the FATAL button (key H). It is a new skill in SKILLS > SUKUNA (1200, it needs the AIR CUT), it works when the enemy is close and at 20% health or less, and it costs nothing.

The scene: the enemy drops to his knees. Sukuna puts a hand in his hair and says "You hold your head quite high" (typed letter by letter at the bottom). A huge slash passes an inch over the kneeling head. The enemy stares up at him, gets up and charges. Sukuna touches his face and is gone: he stands behind him, and the enemy's head falls apart in three slices. Then a slow motion replay shows that Sukuna touched his face before he even reacted, and at normal speed again the enemy falls: K.O. and the round is Sukuna's.

GRAPHIC DAMAGE decides what you see of the cut: FULL shows the slices and the blood, CLEAN the slices without blood, OFF no cut at all (a flash, and he falls). A button pressed after the first second skips to the end (on a phone, tap the screen twice).
Ryu has no FATAL button, so the key H does nothing for him now. Before, it could start Gojo's finisher in a Ryu fight.

t: RYU'S MOVES LOSE THE WORD BLUE
n: The two Ryu moves that had BLUE in their names are renamed, because they are not blue moves: the BLUE PUNCH is the POWER PUNCH and the BLUE COMBO is the 5-HIT COMBO. They are still on the BLUE button, the same as before. The DIVE PUNCH and the DASH KICK never had BLUE in their names. No other fighter has a move with BLUE in its name except Gojo, whose BLUE and MAX BLUE are real blue moves.

t: RYU FIGHTS LIKE A REAL FIGHTER
n: Ryu faces the enemy again (the mirror of V1.162 is gone): his fists and feet go toward the enemy, not behind him.

He steps in so that every blow touches the enemy: the fist or foot meets his body on the hit picture (he closes in up to about 30 steps of distance, and a blow from farther away misses). A blow that hits nothing carries him forward and takes longer to recover from; a blow that lands pushes him back a little, and the heavy ones kick up dust at the enemy's feet. Sparks fly from the place where the blow lands.

The enemy reacts to the blow: a hook snaps his head round, an uppercut lifts him off the floor, a body kick folds him over, a leg kick or a slam puts him on the floor, and the big punches and the dash kick throw him back.

The blows are remade like real mixed martial arts: the hooks and the straight punch turn the hips and the shoulders into the blow, keep the other hand at the chin and reach level with the shoulder (the arm is now fixed to the shoulder, it used to float), and the front kick leans back less. Ryu has five different hurt pictures now: a hit to the head, to the belly, a heavy hit that makes him stagger, a hit that knocks him off his feet and a hit to the legs.

Ryu has the BLUE button now, and its move changes with what he does. Standing it is the BLUE PUNCH: a hard punch with blue light round the fist that sends the enemy flying back. In the air it is the DIVE PUNCH: he flies fast to a place above the enemy and punches him down into the floor, smoke comes up and the enemy is stunned for 1.4 seconds. Holding forward it is the BLUE COMBO: right hook, left hook, uppercut, a kick, and an elbow that pushes the enemy far back.

DASH right after a blue punch or a blue combo is a DASH KICK: press it within half a second of the last blow (or already while the move is on) and Ryu dashes to where the enemy was thrown and kicks him far back. While that works the DASH button says DASH KICK.

Five new animations for him (uppercut, elbow, blue punch, dive punch, dash kick) and a burst of blue light on every blue blow. The blue moves have short cooldowns (0.7 s the punch, 3 s the dive, 2.5 s the combo, 1.5 s the kick), so they cannot be thrown again at once.

Ryu's sprite is mirrored now (left and right swapped): in the fight and on his card in the character select. Only the picture changed: his moves, his reach and the place where his blows hit are exactly as before (in front of him, to the right).

After the blade scene (the hard cut to black) the game now shows the card END OF CHAPTER 4, with the name of the chapter, THE VESSEL, in red under it, and then the card TO BE CONTINUED, and then the chapter menu. On a narrow screen the first card is written in two lines so that the letters keep their size.
Fixed: since V1.157 the TO BE CONTINUED card was never seen: a black layer was drawn over it, so the ending was only a black screen. Both cards show now.
The save slot of a save that has finished chapter 4 says CHAPTER 4 COMPLETE.

t: THE BLADE IS RED AND IN HIS HAND
n: Iron Man's blade is red now and it is fixed to his hand: it grows out of the front of his fist along his arm (with a red flash), with a golden guard where the fist and the blade meet, a bright pink edge, a glint at the point and a red glow round it. Before, it was a thin pale line beside the hand that was cut off at the end, with a glint that floated at a fixed place.
The glint of the blade in Yuji's eye is red too.
He raises his arm first and the blade comes out of the fist: no more jump of the arm. The blade is a little shorter so that its point stops at Yuji's face.

Ranos was glitchy and ugly in V1.158 and is built again from scratch. He is drawn like the other people of the story now (shaded and smooth, no stretched picture), with the look of the figure at the end of chapter 2: purple skin, a bald head with a heavy brow and a square chin (drawn by hand), a dark-blue vest, a belt, dark trousers, long black boots with golden knee guards, and the golden gauntlet with the purple stone.

He moves like a person: he falls feet first down the column of light, lands in a crouch with his fist on the roof, stands up, reaches out with the gauntlet and holds Meguna's fist (a slow sway of the strain), swings his arm to throw him away, turns round, walks up to Yuji with heavy steps (a thud and dust at each), winds up and punches him in the stomach. His arm is bent as far as it needs to reach exactly the fist or the stomach.

Nothing slides or flickers any more: the camera finds Ranos and then stands still (before, it followed the shaking Meguna and moved everything by a pixel now and then), his feet stay where they are, and all moves are blended frame by frame.
A thin violet edge of light (from the moon) round him makes him stand out from the dark city. The banner HALF HEALTH! goes away before he arrives.

Ranos now looks exactly like the figure at the end of chapter 2, the one who blew up the planet: his own picture, a little bigger, with the purple skin, the blue vest, the dark trousers and the golden gauntlet with the purple stone. The helmet and the dark-blue armour of V1.157 are gone.

He no longer steps out of a violet circle: a thin line of violet light comes down out of the sky over the roof, grows into a column of light, and Ranos falls down it and lands between Yuji and Meguna (a flash, a cracked roof, a ring of dust, the screen shakes) and catches Meguna's wrist.

His arm moves now: it reaches out to catch Meguna's fist, swings up to throw him away, and after he has turned and walked up to Yuji it punches down into Yuji's stomach. Then the violet circle takes Yuji to New York and the story goes on as in V1.157 (Iron Man, the blade, TO BE CONTINUED).
The speech boxes of this scene are at the bottom of the screen so that they do not cover Ranos's head.

t: THE STORY GOES ON: RANOS AND NEW YORK
n: Winning or losing the fight against Meguna no longer ends the chapter or shows a defeat screen: both lead to the same scene. (The cutting-down scene with the pieces and the TRY AGAIN screen are gone.)

WIN: the Black Flash that takes Meguna to half health throws him back, he comes back at once with a slash, and Ranos (the one from the end of chapter 2) steps out of a violet circle between them and catches Meguna's wrist with the stone gauntlet: "NOT YET, SUKUNA." - "...YOU?!". LOSS: Meguna's last blow punches Yuji back and he comes in for the slash, and Ranos steps in the same way.
Ranos throws Meguna away, turns to Yuji, says "YOU ARE NEEDED ELSEWHERE." and punches him in the stomach; the purple stone opens a violet circle under Yuji and takes him away (a violet-white flash).

NEW YORK, in daylight: Yuji falls out of the sky onto a freeway, the cars stop and honk at him, he is confused. Iron Man comes down from the sky with a trail of fire, lands in a little crater, and when Yuji asks where he is, a blade slides out of Iron Man's armour: "BACK DOWN, KID... OR YOU GET STABBED." A close-up of Yuji's frightened eye, a hard cut to black, TO BE CONTINUED, and the chapter menu (chapter 4 is marked as finished there).
SKIP is in the corner of every new scene. Sounds: car horns, Iron Man's jets and the blade are new.
Meguna's brain no longer waits for losses to get smarter: it learns while you fight (faster and sharper for every 30 health he loses and every 30 seconds).

t: CHAPTER 4 GOES ON: YUJI VS MEGUNA
n: After the black cut at the end of chapter 4 the game goes straight on (no saves screen any more): the screen fades in from black on the same rooftop city, now in the normal Jujutsu Sorcerers look. Sukuna is in Megumi's body (MEGUNA): black spiky hair, Megumi's dark uniform, Sukuna's face marks and red eyes.

The cutscene (silence, then the fight song from Yuji's first punch): Yuji charges with a glowing fist and punches, Meguna sinks into his shadow, the shadow slides under Yuji's feet and Meguna comes up out of it with an uppercut that throws Yuji up and back, Yuji lands and kicks him away, runs at him screaming and lands a BLACK FLASH, and Sukuna is shocked (a close-up of his face). A few short lines are on screen. SKIP is in the corner.

Then the fight is yours: you are Yuji with the normal buttons (walk, jump, crouch, block, dash) and ONE attack, the BLACK FLASH (the FLASH button): standing = the punch, in the air = the kick to the head, crouched = the blow to the stomach. A ring flashes where the blow goes: if Meguna is still inside it when the fist lands it is a full Black Flash (it breaks a guard); if he has moved out of it, it is a weak punch (a quarter of the damage). All your damage is halved. Bring Meguna to HALF health (the bar has a mark) and the chapter menu opens; the chapter is marked as finished.

Meguna fights with walking, jumping, dashing, blocking and M1 chains of 2 to 4 blows (the last one is a face kick that breaks a guard, and a crouching Yuji ducks it), and rarely the SHADOW SINK (his pool slides under you, a ring warns, and the uppercut that comes up cannot be blocked: dash or jump away). His brain sees you as you were a moment ago, reads the wind-up of your Black Flash and dodges or blocks it, steps in when you miss, remembers what you do (jumps, dashes, long Black Flashes, guarding) and counters it, baits with feints and never stands still inside your reach.

If you lose, Meguna cuts Yuji down with an X slash and he bursts into pieces (GRAPHIC DAMAGE follows your setting: FULL = pieces and blood, CLEAN = slash lines and dark pieces without blood, OFF = slash lines and a cut to black), then TRY AGAIN or MENU. Every loss makes Meguna faster and smarter (up to 6 times); TRY AGAIN skips the cutscene.
Also: a save that has finished chapter 4 now says CHAPTER 4: THE VESSEL.

The ART section (the CUSTOM card on the CHOOSE A MODE screen, where you drew your own characters) is removed completely: the card, the slots, the name screen, the pixel editor, the animation lists, the CODE blocks, the stats page, the test button and the cards for your own fighters on the CHOOSE YOUR FIGHTER screen.
Sukuna and Ryu are not part of it and work as before (they only share the fighting engine that used to live next to the editor).
Characters you drew earlier stay stored on your phone but nothing reads them any more, so they are not shown or playable. They are still inside the save code.

t: SUKUNA CAN DASH, BLOCK, GET HURT AND CROUCH-JUMP
n: DASH: tap DASH. Holding FORWARD he dashes forward 50 px, otherwise he dashes back 42 px (Yuji's own dash pictures with Sukuna's head). It is free, and the enemy's blows miss you for the first part of it, like the other fighters' dashes.
BLOCK: hold BLOCK and his hands go up in front of his face. Blows from the front bounce off, a guard raised just before a blow is a PARRY, and you walk at a third of the speed while it is up.

HURT: when a blow lands he reels in one of seven hit reactions (flinching, thrown back, doubled over, hands on his head, swaying, on his knees) for about half a second and cannot act meanwhile. A blow in the middle of a swing stops it. His moves that cannot be touched (the counter, DISMANTLE, the DASH SLASH, the CLEAVE moves, the FLAME mode and the domain) are not interrupted.
CROUCH JUMP: crouch with the crouch button, then JUMP. He springs up out of the crouch and jumps 30 px high instead of 22.
GRAPHIC DAMAGE: all the new pictures show the limbs he has lost, and so does the AIR CUT, which had no torn-limb pictures before.
Still not there: the MODE moves of the FLAME mode (it has only OPEN), a dash from a crouch and a crouch landing.

t: A BIG GRAPHICS PAGE AND UNLIMITED FPS
n: The GRAPHICS page of the settings screen is rebuilt. At the top: five quality presets (POTATO, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH and ULTRA; it says CUSTOM when you change an option yourself) and a little live picture that shows your options at once. HIGH is exactly how the game looked before. ULTRA adds the extra effects.

LESS (for slower phones): PARTICLES (none, few, some, normal, many), BACKGROUND DETAIL (flat, low, medium, full), AURA AND RINGS (off, flames only, all), SCREEN OVERLAYS (off, light, full), plus screen shake, flash strength, hit pause and damage numbers.

MORE (for fast phones): GLOW (bloom), MOTION TRAILS (fading copies behind fast fighters), SHADOWS AND LIGHT (a shadow under every fighter and a pale pool of light) and MANY particles (more than twice as many).
PICTURE: CAMERA ZOOM (75% to 125%, in fights and free play only), FIXED RETRO SIZE (always 288 x 128 with black bars round it), PIXEL SMOOTHING, brightness, contrast, colour, scanlines and hitboxes.

FRAME RATE: AUTO, 30, 45, 60, 72, 90, 120, 144 and UNLIMITED. The old 60 limit is gone. UNLIMITED has no limit at all, and the app now asks Android for the fastest screen mode your phone has (FPS = pictures the game draws a second, Hz = pictures the screen can show a second), so a 120 Hz phone really gets 120 in the app. The same list is in the pause settings.

TOOLS: a STATS OVERLAY (the FPS, or detailed: how long a picture takes, the screen's rate, the picture size and the quality) and TEST MY PHONE, a 5 second test that finds the preset your phone can handle. The test also runs by itself ONCE on the title screen the first time you start this version and sets that preset (it tells you; change it in SETTINGS, GRAPHICS). Heavy options show a warning under the tools.

t: A BIG SETTINGS SCREEN IN THE MAIN MENU
n: NEW SETTINGS BUTTON on the title screen (top right) and on the CHOOSE A MODE screen. It opens a big screen with pages: GRAPHICS, GAMEPLAY, STORY, SOUND, CONTROLS, ACCESS, LOOK, DATA and PRESETS. Every option has a line that explains it and a DEF button that puts it back to the default. A search box finds any option by its words, and RESET PAGE resets a whole page. All your old settings are still there and the pause-menu settings show the same numbers.

GRAPHICS: screen shake strength, flash strength, hit pause, damage numbers on/off, brightness, contrast, colour (0 = black and white), scanlines, frame rate, battery saver, an FPS counter and hitboxes. GAMEPLAY: assist, game pace (now also SLOW), enemy damage, your damage, health regen, auto-pause and three cheats (infinite energy, infinite health, one-hit kills; not in Wi-Fi fights; while a cheat is on you earn no money).

STORY: subtitles on/off and blood level. ACCESS: reduce flashing, high contrast, colour-blind help, slow motion, bigger buttons. LOOK: six menu colours. SOUND: every volume plus the sound switch. CONTROLS: button size, opacity, height, side, vibration.

DATA: your play time, fights won and lost, hits landed, parries and story chapter; the save code, a SETTINGS-ONLY code you can share, reset stats, reset settings and reset all progress (asks twice). PRESETS: DEFAULT, BATTERY, PERFORMANCE, CINEMATIC, CASUAL and HARDCORE in one tap.

t: CHAPTER 4: THE HANDS ARE NOW REAL 3D HANDS
n: THE HANDS OF THE FINGER RIP ARE DRAWN AGAIN, THIS TIME AS REAL HANDS: every hand is built from bones, knuckles, nails and skin as a small 3D model, lit from the upper left with soft shadows between the fingers, and turned into the game's pixel art. They look like real hands now (knuckles, tendons, the webs between the fingers, nails, the sleeve), not like flat shapes.

THE RIP: Sukuna's hand holds Megumi's face (you see his face, dark, behind it) with the little finger stuck out, and his other hand pinches it from below and pulls. The skin of the hand stretches and goes pale, then the finger tears off. With blood on you see the raw hole with the blood running down his hand; with blood off it is a clean wound. The other hand takes the finger away.

THE RIPPED FINGER close-up is a real finger with a torn end (ragged skin, red flesh, the white bone), held between a thumb and a first finger; it turns dark red while the black claw grows out of its nail. Yuji's open hand without its little finger is a real hand too.

t: CHAPTER 4: HUMAN SKIN COLOURS AND A REALISTIC HAND FOR THE FINGER RIP
n: THE FACES HAVE A HUMAN COLOUR: Sukuna, Yuji and Megumi now have warm peach skin with red-brown shadows (before it was a dull brown and a grey). When they are frightened the skin goes pale and cool but still looks like skin, not stone. The dark layer over the close-ups is much lighter, so the colours show.

THE HAND THAT RIPS THE FINGER IS REDRAWN FROM THE START: a real hand with the proper shape and proportions: knuckles with wrinkles, the tendons on the back, jointed fingers with creases, real nails (pink with a half moon and a white edge), a shaded wrist and the blue sleeve. It holds Megumi's face (you see his face behind it, out of focus), the little finger sticks out and his other hand pinches it, then pulls: the skin of the hand stretches between the knuckle and the finger, turns pale, splits, and the finger comes off. With blood on, the stump is raw red flesh with the white of the bone and the blood runs down his hand; with blood off it is a clean pink stump.

THE RIPPED FINGER AND YUJI'S HAND ARE REDRAWN TOO: the finger between his thumb and first finger is a real finger (nail, creases, a ragged torn end with the bone) that turns dark red and cracked while the black claw grows; the same red finger is what goes into Megumi's mouth. Yuji's hand without its little finger is a real open hand with the lines of the palm. All the fingers of Sukuna on Megumi's cheek, mouth and throat now have real nails, creases and shading.

t: CHAPTER 4: MORE MASCULINE FACES, NO TEARS, AND A TRAUMATISED MEGUMI AND YUJI
n: EVERY FACE NOW LOOKS LIKE A MAN: a longer, squarer jaw with a bevelled chin, a thick neck with its tendons showing, heavy straight brows, narrower sharper eyes with no lashes, a bigger nose with a light edge on the bridge, thin lips with no shine, a day of beard on the jaw, bigger ears and shorter hair (Megumi's fringe stops above his brows and there are no long locks along the cheeks). Sukuna's robe opens in a deep V. The eye, mouth and neck close-ups got the same changes.
NO MORE TEARS: Megumi and Yuji do not cry anywhere in the chapter any more (the gag, the scream, the open mouth, Yuji's eyes, his frightened face and his quiet face).

MEGUMI AND YUJI LOOK TRAUMATISED: the skin goes pale and grey, dark rings grow under the eyes, the eyes open wide with a small iris in a bloodshot white, a pin of a pupil and no light in it (a dead stare), the mouth hangs open, they sweat and they shake. Megumi stares wide-eyed while he gags and screams; Yuji's eye, his frightened face and his quiet face afterwards are the same blank, white-faced stare.

t: NEW FACES: THE CLOSE-UPS OF CHAPTER 4 REDRAWN, AND YUJI KEEPS HIS PINK HAIR
n: YUJI'S HAIR IS THE SAME AS SUKUNA'S: when Sukuna leaves, the hair stays pink (it no longer turns orange). The marks fade, the extra eyes close and the eyes turn from red to brown, as before.

ALL THE CLOSE-UP FACES ARE REDRAWN, much bigger and more detailed, in the game's own pixel size: Sukuna (narrow red eyes, the extra pair of eyes, the marks, a smirk with a fang, a wide grin), Yuji (big brown eyes, thick brows, fear, tears, quiet sadness) and Megumi (long lashes, the fringe of black hair, his scream with the eyes shut, the face that rises out of the dark with Sukuna's marks, red eyes and smile). Real shading, a dark edge on the shadow side, lids, lashes, nose, lips and teeth.

THE EYE CLOSE-UPS ARE REDRAWN: iris fibres, a wet light, veins in the white, lashes, the brow with its hairs, tears and sweat, and Sukuna's face (or Megumi's) as a tiny reflection in the eye. Sukuna's fingers on the cheek are drawn properly too.

THE MOUTH CLOSE-UP IS REDRAWN: his jaw pulled open by Sukuna's fingers, teeth, tongue, strings of spit, tears, and the red finger with the long black nail going in. The swallow (his throat, the lump going down), his head hanging with the hair over his face, Sukuna's hand on his jaw pulling his little finger, the red finger with the black nail and Yuji's hand without its little finger are redrawn in the same style.

t: CHAPTER 4, PART 2: THE FINGER, THE SCREAM AND THE SMILE
n: THE STORY GOES ON from the moment Sukuna holds Megumi by the jaw, with no black card, all the way to the end of your song (about 2 and a half more minutes, 28 shots, every one with something new). His left hand leaves his pocket and takes the little finger of his own right hand. He pulls and it comes off (GRAPHIC DAMAGE: FULL shows the blood, CLEAN shows none, OFF cuts away from the tearing). In close-up the finger turns red and a long black nail grows out of it.

HE FORCES MEGUMI'S JAW OPEN and pushes the finger in (slow motion as it goes in). Megumi gags, tears run, his whole body shakes, and he screams: a muffled scream under the organ. Then the swallow. Sukuna lets go and Megumi falls on his knees with his head down and the hair over his face.

SUKUNA LEAVES YUJI'S BODY: the pink hair turns orange, the marks fade and the red eyes turn brown. Yuji sees his missing finger, looks at Megumi, steps back in horror and whispers "FUSHIGURO...?". A long silence, his hand shakes a hand's breadth from Megumi's hair.

THEN MEGUMI SLOWLY LIFTS HIS HEAD: the hair falls aside, Sukuna's marks appear on his face, his eyes turn red with a second pair of eyes under them, and he smiles Sukuna's smile on the loudest swell of the song. No words. A hard cut to black on the last swell and you are straight back at the saves. Reaching the end is remembered on your save.

t: CHAPTER 4 MADE REALISTIC: A MUCH FASTER CHASE AND A NEW SUKUNA
n: THE CHASE IS ABOUT TWICE AS FAST: Megumi sprints, the jump is quicker and snappier, the roofs and the skyline rush past and there are no empty stretches any more (the things on the roofs come from a recipe: jump over crates, vents and air conditioners, slide under pipes, washing lines and water tanks, jump the gaps (the wide ones need a held jump), two crates in a row, a pipe followed by a crate). The slashes and the cuts in the roofs are gone. You still cannot lose.

A NEW SUKUNA, like the manga (Yuji's body): short spiky pink hair, the high red hood round his neck, the dark uniform with gold buttons, a narrow red eye, a second pair of eyes and the marks on his face. He is no longer a black shape: he runs and leaps on the far roofs, then right behind Megumi, jumping the same gaps and crates and closing in when you stumble. From 2:37 he gains on Megumi for good.

THE CATCH IS BELIEVABLE NOW: no flying, no teleport, no afterimages. Sukuna runs up behind Megumi, leaps over him in a long jump (slow motion), lands in a crouch in the dust, stands up and turns round. Megumi skids, backs away, turns and runs; Sukuna runs after him, takes him by the collar and swings him round. Then his hand, on a normal arm that is bent a little, closes on Megumi's jaw and cheeks and lifts him a little off the roof. You see them in colour, Megumi's eye with the fingers on his cheek, his boots, and Sukuna's face looking down at him with a calm smirk. Hard cut to black on the last swell, as before.
A swipe down in the middle of a jump now cuts the jump short and slides.

t: CHAPTER 4: THE VESSEL (PART 1): THE ROOFTOP CHASE AND THE CATCH
n: A new story chapter after chapter 3: THE VESSEL. Open it from CONTINUE / CHOOSE CHAPTER in the saves screen, or go straight on from the end of chapter 3. It is made to the whole of your song (L'AMOUR TOUJOURS, the slowed organ). This first part runs to 3:19 and ends with TO BE CONTINUED; the rest (the finger, Yuji, the smile) comes in the next update.

THE AFTERMATH: Megumi kneels, bleeding, in the ruins of the wheel and gets up. Sukuna steps out of the smoke on the swell of the organ, walks to him while the camera cuts between his boots, Megumi's face and the whole roof, and says RUN. Megumi turns and runs.

THE CHASE (about 2 minutes, you play it): Megumi runs across the rooftops by himself. TAP = JUMP (hold = higher), SWIPE DOWN or tap the LEFT side of the screen = SLIDE (keys: Space / Up = jump, Down = slide). Jump over crates, vents and air conditioners and over the gaps (the wide gaps need a held jump); slide under pipes, washing lines and water tanks. Sukuna's slashes cut the roof in front of you (a moment of slow motion) and sweep in from behind at head height. You cannot lose: a stumble only slows Megumi and drops him back on the screen, Sukuna comes closer, the heartbeat speeds up and the edges of the screen go red. The place changes as you run: the rooftops, a crane, glass towers, the collapse; a black shape runs and leaps along the far roofs.

THE CATCH: in slow motion a black shape leaps over the moon and falls in front of Megumi. He skids, turns and runs, a flash, and Sukuna is in front of him. He backs away, and a hand clamps over his face: a black two-shot against the moon, his eye (twice), his boots kicking in the air, Sukuna's face grinning in the dark. Hard cut to black on the last swell of the song. Blood on Megumi follows the GRAPHIC DAMAGE setting (only on FULL). SKIP jumps to the next part. Everything is pixel art.

t: RYU REDONE: REAL POSES, SWINGING CLOTH AND HAIR, HURT AND K.O.
n: Ryu no longer stays in the pose of your picture. Your picture is now only his LOOK (face, hair, fur, jacket, belt, jeans, boots) and every animation is posed fresh. The idle is a boxer's bounce on bent knees with his weight going from one foot to the other. The walk is a heavy stomp: a foot comes up slowly and comes down hard, his body rocks and drops on every step, with a puff of dust, the sound of a step and a hair of screen shake. Walking back is the same stomp, backing away with his guard up.

His hair, the white fur of the collar and the cuffs, the open jacket with its spiky tail and his jeans swing on their own now: they lag behind when he moves and swing back, stronger on fast moves. His waist bends too, so his chest and his hips can turn against each other, and his knees bend smoothly.

New poses: the jump tucks his knees up; the crouch is ONE KNEE DOWN (the crouch walk is a low crawl-step); the block is a high guard with both forearms up; the dash is a shoulder charge (head down, jacket flying behind him, smudge and speed lines, forwards and backwards). Every blow has its own style: boxing hooks, a capoeira rising kick, an anime flying punch, a Muay Thai low kick and push kick, a pro-wrestling overhead slam and a karate straight punch.

He has HURT and K.O. pictures now: he flinches when you are hit and falls on his back when you lose. A small change you may feel: the JUMP PUNCH now travels 24 px forward and the KICK UP throws the enemy 44 px up (it was 60), so KICK UP then JUMP PUNCH still connects.

Ryu Ishigori joins FREE PLAY: pick RYU on the fighter select screen (next to Sukuna). He is the big, heavy brawler from the pixel design you chose, and every one of his animations has 15 pictures: idle, walk, walk back, jump, crouch, crouch idle, crouch walk, block, dash and all of his blows. When he moves fast he gets action lines on his body.

What ATTACK does depends on what you are doing. Standing still, tap it again and again (each tap within 0.7 seconds of the last) for the chain: LEFT HOOK, RIGHT HOOK, KICK UP (the enemy flies up) and JUMP PUNCH (he hops and punches forward, it can even hit the enemy you just kicked up, and sends him flying forward). Crouched: LEG KICK, he kicks the enemy's legs out from under him. In the air: DOWNSLAM, both fists drive down onto the enemy. Holding FORWARD: HARD PUNCH, a lunge that sends the enemy back. Holding BACK: FRONT KICK, he kicks forward. The ATTACK button always shows the name of the blow that comes next.

DASH takes 0.2 seconds (the stat DASH TIME says 200 MS; the default FAST game pace makes everything a quarter quicker) and its middle pictures are smudged with blue speed trails and action lines, forwards and backwards. BLOCK uses both hands. Ryu walks slower than the others (46 against 56) and has 340 health instead of 300. The buttons he does not use (BLUE, MODE, DOMAIN, FATAL) are hidden while he fights.

t: CONTINUE OR CHOOSE A CHAPTER IN STORY MODE
n: After you pick a save in STORY MODE you now get two buttons: CONTINUE (goes on where you stopped, as before) and CHOOSE CHAPTER. The chapter list shows Chapter 1 (The Mystery), Chapter 2 (The Portal) and Chapter 3 (The Divine General). Chapters your save has not reached yet are greyed out and say LOCKED. An empty save still just says START.

Replaying an earlier chapter never takes progress away: CONTINUE still goes to your furthest chapter. The BACK button (and the phone's back button) steps from the chapter list back to the saves. Chapter 3 now always starts its quick time events fresh, so the how-to-play card and the score come again when you replay it.

t: A FIGHT THAT NEVER STOPS: HOW-TO-PLAY CARD, HOLD AND MASH PROMPTS, AND THE WHOLE CITY AS THE ARENA
n: A how-to-play card now comes before the first ring of the air fight: an animated TAP ring and an animated HOLD ring, and the rules in plain words. TAP when the circle reaches the middle circle: Sukuna dodges Mahoraga. HOLD when Sukuna attacks: press when the ring appears and let go exactly when it reaches the middle circle. Tap the screen (after a second) to start. It comes every time the fight starts, also after DEFEATED.

New prompts. Every blow of Sukuna now asks for a HOLD (orange ring, the middle turns green while your finger is down); miss it and Mahoraga blocks, Sukuna cannot attack for a moment and Mahoraga gets the upper hand with a blow of his own. The clashes ask you to MASH (tap five times fast). The throw asks for three SWIPES (up, left, down); a missed swipe smashes Sukuna through the wall the ragged way, with blood. Taps, holds, mashes and swipes all count the same toward the 75% you need, and more than 3 misses still brings the flurry.

The fight is action only now: no more calm and no more face-offs between the blows, a blow every beat or two, and every camera cut is a new angle. The city is the arena: a chase through three skyscrapers (the glass breaks as they go through), Sukuna cuts a whole tower in half and they fight beside its falling top, which crashes through the roof of the next building; they fall through its floors as it comes down (each floor breaks under them), Mahoraga throws Sukuna back through the buildings, they land on a rooftop with a water tower where the wheel learns Sukuna's slash (THE WHEEL ADAPTS), and then it is straight up through the clouds to a huge moon, up to the last kick.

The camera keeps both fighters in the picture (nobody is thrown out of the shot any more) and follows a lunge smoothly. Fixed: the score counter and the SKIP button of the quick time events were hidden under the black cinema bars; they now show in the top bar.

t: QUICK TIME EVENTS IN THE AIR FIGHT: DODGE MAHORAGA'S BLOWS
n: Now you fight too. Every time Mahoraga is about to hit Sukuna in the air fight (the first punch in the slow motion and then each of his hooks, kicks and punches) a ring closes on Sukuna: TAP anywhere as it closes (the ring turns gold at the perfect moment). A tap in time makes Sukuna dodge, block or meet the fist; PERFECT, GOOD, TOO EARLY or MISS shows. A counter in the corner shows how many you got.

If you miss, the story branches a little: the blow lands and throws Sukuna back, he cannot attack for a few seconds (his next blows are cancelled), and Mahoraga follows up with one more blow (with its own prompt). Then the fight goes back to normal.
If you miss MORE THAN 3 times, Mahoraga attacks again and again: a flurry of blows on every beat of the song (5 at the 4th miss, 2 more every time you miss after that), each with its own prompt.

At the end of the fight (just before the last kick) the game counts your taps. Under 75% and Sukuna is overwhelmed: DEFEATED, and the air fight starts again from the beginning. 75% or more and the story goes on as before. A SKIP button in the corner skips a cut (and counts for nothing).

t: A LOT MORE SLASHES IN THE DOMAIN, AND THE BLOOD IS BLOWN AWAY BY THE WIND
n: The rain of slashes in Sukuna's domain is about four times as thick and much more violent: long thick cuts everywhere, a huge burst with every heavy hit of the song (and a red flash), many more cuts landing on Mahoraga, and the screen shakes hard all the time.

When Mahoraga comes apart in the first domain shot, his blood no longer falls to the floor: a strong wind blows it away to the right in streaks that get faster and faster until the screen is empty, with streaks of wind across the picture and the sound of the gust.

t: MAHORAGA WALKS ON WITH HIS ARMS COMING UP, SLOWLY AND HURT
n: At the big hit at 2:03 Mahoraga no longer stops. He keeps walking forward in short, dragging, painful steps (his feet really step on the ground and never slide) while his arms come up very slowly: one tenth more with every heavy hit of the song, ten hits in all, from hanging at his sides to both open hands held out in front of him. His head hangs, his body is bent, his arms tremble, and he gets slower and slower until he stops just before the lull.

He starts farther away now (he kneels about 470 px from Sukuna) so that he can walk the whole way. The slashes, the steam and the regrowing go on exactly as before, and the leap and the arrow are unchanged.
New: ten shuffle pictures sets for Mahoraga (gs1 - gs10), a new speed for the whole walk (a slow start, steady, a little slower at 2:03, then slower and slower).

t: SUKUNA VS MAHORAGA, PART 4: THE SNOWMAN (THE END OF THE DOMAIN)
n: After the blood there is a short silence while the camera looks down from the red sky and the moon to the floor of the domain and finds Mahoraga on one knee in his own blood. The second song (Snowman, from 1:21 to its end) hits as he is found, and the whole part is timed to it: every heavy hit of the song (one every 1.7 seconds) is a hit of the domain.

Mahoraga stands up in the rain of Sukuna's slashes and is cut to ribbons, covered in red wounds that bleed. The wheel turns again and again (he adapts, the old wounds close) but it is too much, so he walks forward through the rain, leaving blood behind him, while the shrine slides in behind Sukuna, until the big hit at 2:03.

At 2:03 he lifts both hands to shield himself. Every heavy hit blows his body apart into steam and he grows back before the next one, ten times in a row. Then the song thins out, Sukuna lights the fire in his hands (FUGA), Mahoraga crouches and jumps up to punch, and the arrow hits him in the face: the head is gone, the body falls and burns away, the wheel breaks, and the domain goes dark as the song ends. The chapter card follows.

New: Mahoraga's kneel, stand-up, hunched walk, hands-up and guard pictures, the endless slash rain, wounds and blood trails, the steam and the fire, 36 camera shots (every tap still skips one). The song is a real recording inside the game files, so keep the game to yourself.

t: SUKUNA VS MAHORAGA, PART 3: THE AIR FIGHT TO 2:00, THE SONG STOPS, THE DOMAIN
n: The air fight goes on to the end of the first two minutes of the song, every blow on a beat. Mahoraga throws hooks with both arms and a high kick, Sukuna dodges, blocks and hits back with jabs, a kick and a cut, and the fists meet in three big clashes. They fall together through the clouds to the roofs of the city (a long calm there while the song breaks down, the wheel turning again and again), climb back to the moon, and the big hits flash in black and white.

At 2:00 Sukuna dodges a hook and punches Mahoraga in the face, Mahoraga kicks him back, and the song STOPS dead as the kick lands. In silence Sukuna flies far back, makes the domain hand sign with red energy streaming into his fingers, and your GIF (turned into pixel art, all 38 frames) fills the whole screen while DOMAIN EXPANSION / MALEVOLENT SHRINE is written on it. The red domain spreads out of him, the shrine rises, and Mahoraga comes apart into blood that rains on the floor. The chapter card follows; the Snowman part (Mahoraga on one knee, the rain of slashes, Fuga) comes in the next update.

New: Mahoraga's hook (two arms), kick and hurt pictures, 27 scripted blows with impact flashes, shakes, sparks and blood, the calm with drifting embers, the GIF in pixel form, the domain circle and the dissolving into blood. Taps still skip cut by cut. The song is a real recording inside the game files, so keep the game to yourself.

t: SUKUNA VS MAHORAGA, PART 2: THE AIR FIGHT (FIRST HALF, WITH MUSIC)
n: Chapter 3 goes on high above the city. Sukuna finds his balance in the air while Mahoraga looks up from the street, crouches and leaps all the way up to him. The song "I Will Survive" fades in (the first two minutes of it are in the game) and every big hit lands on its beat.

Mahoraga's punch comes in BULLET TIME: the world slows to a crawl and the camera swings round while Sukuna leans out of the way. Then the snap: Sukuna cuts Mahoraga's arm off (a black-and-white impact flash) and kicks it away. Mahoraga grabs Sukuna with his other hand and throws him down. Sukuna's slashes catch Mahoraga like a red-and-white rope, he spins him round and round while the arm grows back, and throws him up into the sky. Sukuna rises after him and the scene stops there; the rest of the two minutes (hooks, trading blows in the air, the kick down to the street, the crash and the huge Mahoraga floating over Sukuna) comes in the next update.

New: Mahoraga's leap, hover, flying punch, stump, open hand, throw and growing-arm pictures; Sukuna's air pictures (balance, beckon, lean back, chop, pulling the rope, throwing); about 40 seconds of new scene with clouds, wind, blood, impact flashes and slow motion that also slows the music. Taps still skip cut by cut and the music jumps with them. The song is a real recording and it is inside the game files, so keep the game to yourself.

Chapter 3 goes on after "THIS BRAT IS A PAIN IN THE ASS". Sukuna gets up in the alley, rolls his neck, looks around and sees Mahoraga far away. Mahoraga charges; Sukuna steps back and the punch hits only the air; then Sukuna dashes in and cuts him to pieces with an X slash and walks away. The wheel turns, the pieces fly back together and Mahoraga is whole again. Sukuna looks back, and Mahoraga's uppercut sends him flying up over the roofs of the city, past a huge moon.

Sukuna has three new lines (A SHIKIGAMI? HOW CUTE. / TOO EASY. / OH? THE WHEEL TURNS... HOW AMUSING.). New: Mahoraga's run, lunge and uppercut pictures, a night sky with stars, a huge moon and the lit towers of the city over the alley, and a few new sounds. Taps still skip cut by cut. The fight in the air and the huge Mahoraga floating over Sukuna come in the next update.

Chapter 3 has a new ending. After Verity is killed the camera cuts to the alley, where Yuji lies in the crater with his belly torn open. The wound slowly closes, the organs that came out fly back in one by one, his heart starts to beat and he opens his eyes. The camera goes up to them: they are red, and the body is Sukuna's now (his head, his face marks). He says: THIS BRAT IS A PAIN IN THE ASS. Then the chapter card comes (TO BE CONTINUED).
A tap still skips: the first tap goes to the moment the eyes open, the next one to the card. New sounds: the heartbeat, the wet sounds of the organs and the wound, and Sukuna's deep voice.

Verity has the RCT now, with four stages (the fourth is only his): $1500, $2500, $4000 and $8000. You need his FATALITY first, and each stage needs the one before. A hurt part (a ripped off limb, a dead shoulder, a hurt chest, belly or head) is whole again after: stage 1: 10 seconds, stage 2: 5 seconds, stage 3: 1 second, stage 4: at once. At stage 4 a torn piece still flies off, but his body is whole again the moment the hit is over, and the piece is taken back a moment later. In free play Verity has all four stages.

Verity's body is the most fragile one in the game: every blow fills his body's damage 3 times as fast as anyone else's, and a hard blow can rip a piece off at once much more often. This is true for the enemy Verity too, and it does not matter whether you bought the RCT.

Sukuna is in the shop now. He costs $3000 (SKILLS > CHARACTERS) and until you buy him his card in free play is locked. Once he is yours, the SUKUNA tab sells his moves, and they are locked until you buy them, free play too. Walking, jumping and his first blows (jab, jab, kick and the counter) stay free.

The moves, with their prices: CROUCH $50, CROUCH PUNCHES $120 (needs CROUCH), FLYING SLASHES $150 (ATTACK with no enemy near), AIR CUT $250 (BLUE), CUT STORM $400 (back + BLUE), LEG CUT $300 (crouch + BLUE), DISMANTLE $600 (jump + BLUE), DASH SLASH $500 (forward + BLUE), CLEAVE MODE $700 (the MODE button), LIFT CLEAVE $300, DIVE CLEAVE $350 and DASH CLEAVE $400 (all three in Cleave mode), FLAME MODE $900 (MODE again, BLUE is OPEN), MALEVOLENT SHRINE $2000 (the DOMAIN button), FUGA $2500 (Flame mode + BLUE while the domain is open), and the three RCT stages. A move you have not bought shows LOCKED: BUY IT IN SKILLS when you press it. If a BLUE variant is not bought, BLUE does the plain AIR CUT instead.
Everyone else is unchanged: in free play all the moves of Gojo, Yuji, Verity and the Cat are still free. Old saves have to buy Sukuna again.

There is a new CODES button on the title screen (bottom right). It opens a page with a box where you type a code and press REDEEM (or Enter). A right code gives you money: Diddy25 gives $1000, Gojo69Me gives $700, and the very long one (PutinKimjongUnDiddyDaddyPeopleNightyNighty) gives $1,000,000. Type them exactly as written, capital letters too.
Each code works once; typing it again says ALREADY USED. Your money and the used codes are saved on the phone, so a used code stays used after you close the game.

RCT (reverse cursed technique) is a new skill for Gojo, Yuji, the Cartoon Cat and Sukuna: white cursed energy heals your injuries, meaning ripped off arms and legs, dead shoulders and a hurt chest, belly or head from GRAPHIC DAMAGE. It does not give health back. You need the FATALITY first (Yuji needs INHERITENCE too; Sukuna needs nothing first because he has no fatality) and it has three expensive stages: $1500, $2500 and $4000. Sukuna has a new SUKUNA tab in SKILLS for his stages, and they are really bought even in free play.

How long a hurt part takes to heal. Stage 1: Gojo 15 seconds, Sukuna 15, Yuji 20, Cat 20. Stage 2: Gojo 10, Sukuna 8, Yuji 16, Cat 14. Stage 3: Gojo under 5 seconds and Sukuna 4 or less (the worse the injury the longer it takes, a small one is healed almost at once), Yuji 10, Cat 7. Every hurt part has its own clock, which starts when it is hurt. Yuji's RCT only starts while INHERITENCE is on (a heal that has started goes on after it ends).

While a fighter heals, a white halo glows round him, white specks rise off him, and a lost limb grows back slowly from the stump outwards, white at first. When a lost limb is whole again, the old piece on the floor is taken back into the energy. In free play, Gojo, Yuji and the Cat have all three stages, like all their other moves.
Fixed: the GRAPHIC DAMAGE setting (FULL / CLEAN / OFF) was forgotten every time the game was closed. It is kept now.

Fighters can now lose their arms and legs (everywhere except Story Mode: Free play, Challenges and Versus). Every body has hidden damage on its arms, legs, shoulders, chest, belly and head. Where a blow lands decides which part takes it (high, middle or low), and cuts, claws and bites (Sukuna, Freddy, Verity) fill it twice as fast. A part that has taken enough, or a rare huge hit, rips off: the piece flies away and lies on the floor until the round ends, blood sprays, the screen flashes red, the game slows down for a moment and the body bleeds a little every half second until the round is over. A badly hurt shoulder leaves the arm hanging limp and useless. A badly hurt chest, belly or head shows wounds, makes the fighter slower and weaker, makes him cough blood now and then (stunned for half a second) and he takes 25% more damage.

What a fighter can still do: with one arm gone only the swings that do not need it work (Yuji and Gojo check every move, and a swing of the lost arm is done by the other one; the other fighters keep all their moves), with no arms there are no hand moves, no blocking and no BLUE, MODE or DOMAIN, and ATTACK becomes a new HEADBUTT. With one leg he hops at 35% speed and cannot jump, kick or dash. With no legs he crawls along the floor at 15% speed and cannot block, jump or dash. Hand-sign domains (Gojo, Yuji, Sukuna, the Cat) need both hands. Verity as the smoke ball is not affected, and a crawler who was crouched when his legs went gets up by himself. Enemies follow the same rules: one without arms headbutts you.

At the end of every FATALITY the loser's head is ripped off. Everything grows back at the start of the next round. SETTINGS > GAME > GRAPHIC DAMAGE has three levels: FULL, CLEAN (no blood: the parts just pop off and fade) and OFF.

If Sukuna uses FUGA (the OPEN fire arrow of FLAME mode, the BLUE button) while his domain is open, it is now a special cutscene of about 12 seconds with nine camera shots: a wide shot of the domain, a close-up of the clap, a tilted shot while the fire plays like slime, a shot from the enemy's side with Sukuna's dark shape in front of it, a close-up of his face while he draws the arrow, a tracking shot that runs ahead of the huge arrow with the word FUGA, the moment it lands (the game stops for an instant in a black and white frame), a fireball and a slow motion close-up on the enemy, a look up at the shrine over the fire, and a slow pull back. Black bars slide in and the health bars and buttons hide while it plays; two taps on the screen (or a button) skip it.

FUGA costs the normal 50% of your energy, and your energy comes back 1% every second, so you can afford it in the last seconds of the 20 second domain. The arrow takes 40% of the enemy's full health and burns him for 8 seconds. The 20 seconds of the domain stand still during the cutscene, the enemy is held and slides to stand in front of Sukuna, and the BLUE button says FUGA instead of OPEN while the domain is open. Outside the domain OPEN works as before.

While Sukuna makes the hand sign, the pixel picture of his face now grows until it covers the whole screen. It appears small behind him, hangs there for a moment, and then zooms in until the city is gone and the face fills the screen from edge to edge: his red eyes, the mark on his forehead and his hands pressed together. As it grows it turns into a sharper 128 x 128 picture of the same face (twice the detail), because a 64 x 64 picture blown up to the whole screen only looks like big blocks. A short knock shakes the screen when it covers everything. When the domain opens, the red domain spreads over the face and the shrine rises, as before.

The order of the layers is fixed and checked: the ground is at the very back, then Sukuna's picture (the face, then the domain with the shrine), then everything else in front of it: the enemy, Sukuna, his effects, the slashes and sparks, and the health bars. The two words DOMAIN EXPANSION and MALEVOLENT SHRINE moved to the floor under the fighters so that they do not hide the face, and the passers-by are hidden as soon as the face shows.

When Sukuna's domain opens, a circle of it spreads out from the fight until it covers the whole screen. The city, the street and the people in it are gone: only Sukuna, the enemy and their effects (the slashes, sparks and blood) are on the screen, in front of the domain. The domain is a blood-red sky with a dark moon, spires of bone and a floor of skulls, and the big pixel picture of the shrine (your second picture) stands in the middle of it, as tall as the screen allows.

The shrine now stays exactly where it is. It comes up out of the ground once, does not drift when Sukuna walks and does not wobble. When the 20 seconds are over, or the enemy goes down, the shrine sinks, the domain shrinks away and the city comes back. The face picture is still a short cut-in while he makes the hand sign. Nothing else changed: 1% of the enemy's health every half second for 20 seconds.

The DOMAIN button is Sukuna's ULTIMATE now. It costs 67% of your energy and can be used again 30 seconds after the domain has ended. Press it and he makes the hand sign: both hands in front of his chin, the two middle fingers touching, while a pixel picture of his face (64 x 64, 16 bit style, from your picture) appears behind him.

Then the domain opens: a shrine with horns and two mouths (your second picture, in pixel style) rises out of the ground behind him, with cracks, dust and rubble. The map stays the same, but slashes cut across the whole screen, many every second, and the words DOMAIN EXPANSION and MALEVOLENT SHRINE are written behind the fighters.

For 20 seconds the enemy loses 1% of his health every half second (40 cuts, 40% in all). Nothing can block or dodge it, and a smoke ball takes nothing. The enemy is held only while Sukuna makes the sign; after that you can walk, jump, attack and use BLUE and MODE all the time. The shrine sinks back into the ground when the 20 seconds are over, or when the enemy goes down or the round ends.

In Sukuna's FLAME mode BLUE is now always OPEN and nothing else. His other BLUE moves (Leg Cut, Dismantle, Cut Storm, Dash Slash and Air Cut) are not in this mode any more. Standing or crouched, BLUE casts OPEN (from the crouch he stands up first). In the air BLUE does nothing.

In FLAME mode the ATTACK button no longer throws flying slashes. It is the punch chain (right jab, left jab, face kick and the counter) whether the enemy is near or far. Crouched he still throws his crouch punches.

The bow of flame and its string are gone from Sukuna's OPEN move. He still takes the pose of an archer, but now only the fire arrow is drawn: it is held at his cheek by his back hand, grows as he draws it, and flies off when he lets go of it. Everything else about OPEN is the same.

t: FIRE ARROW IS NOW A FLAME
n: The fire arrow of Sukuna's FLAME mode is smaller now, and it is made of flame instead of having the shape of an arrow: a round bright head with flame tongues streaming back behind it, and no point. It has 10 frames of idle animation that loop, so the flames keep flickering while it flies. It is still painted in 14 shades of orange, from cream to dark rust.
Everything else about OPEN is the same: the bow pose, the flame that grows on the string, the burn of 1 damage every half second for 8 seconds, and the guard that cannot stop it.

Sukuna has a second mode, FLAME. Tap the MODE button once for CLEAVE, twice for FLAME, and a third time to turn the modes off. In FLAME mode the MODE button and the BLUE button turn orange, and standing BLUE is called OPEN. Crouched, BLUE is still the LEG CUT and in the air it is still DISMANTLE (in orange too). The mode switches itself off at the start of every round.

OPEN costs 50% of the cursed energy and takes about 3 seconds. Flames light on his hands while he says "Wanna See Something Cool?". He lifts his hands and claps them, and the flames flare up. Then he plays with the fire like slime and stretches it between his hands. Then he takes the pose of an archer, with a bow of flame in his front hand and an arrow on the string at his cheek. He lets go with his back hand and a huge fire arrow flies across the screen.

The arrow is huge and painted in 14 shades of orange, from cream to dark rust. No guard can stop it, but an enemy who jumps high, lies down or dashes out of its way is missed. An enemy it hits BURNS: exactly 1 damage every half second for 8 seconds, 16 in all. A second arrow restarts the 8 seconds, the burns do not add up.
While he casts, the enemy can move around and fight, but nothing can touch Sukuna, and the cast always finishes.

Sukuna has a new MODE called CLEAVE. Tap the MODE button to switch it on or off. The switch is silent: nothing is heard, said or shown on the screen, so the enemy cannot tell that he switched. Only your own buttons change (the MODE button lights up and says CLEAVE, and ATTACK and BLUE get new names). The mode switches itself off at the start of every round.

In CLEAVE mode ATTACK is a melee chain: R.HOOK, L.HOOK, ELBOW, and then TOUCH CUT, where Sukuna lays a hand on the enemy and slashes him. The TOUCH CUT takes exactly 1% of the enemy's full health, and a guard can block it. The chain is the same whether the enemy is close or far, and when he is crouched he still throws his crouch punches.

BLUE becomes CLEAVE (5 energy): the same touch and slash, but it takes exactly 5% of the enemy's full health and it breaks a guard. It changes with what you do. Crouch and tap BLUE for LIFT CLEAVE: he lifts the enemy off the floor with one hand and slashes his head. Jump and tap BLUE in the air for DIVE CLEAVE: he drops on the enemy, grabs him and cleaves him to the ground, and the enemy is knocked down. Hold forward with the enemy within 120 pixels and tap BLUE for DASH CLEAVE: he dashes at the enemy and cleaves him back, so the enemy hops and flies away. The LIFT, the DIVE and the DASH cost 10 energy each.
Nothing can touch Sukuna during the LIFT, the DIVE and the DASH. All his old BLUE moves (AIR CUT, CUT STORM, LEG CUT, DISMANTLE and DASH SLASH) are still there when the mode is off.

Sukuna has a new slash move, DASH SLASH. Walk forward and tap the BLUE button (it is called DASH SLASH now when you hold forward with the enemy close) and he dashes straight through the enemy and stops behind him. While he stands there the enemy stands still and does not even turn round.

Then the whole game freezes for 1.23 seconds. First an impact frame flashes: the screen goes black and white with rays and one thick white slash across the enemy. Then the normal picture comes back, frozen, and a red and white cut opens across the enemy while the first drops of blood fall.

When the game goes on again the cut lands: a little damage (20) and two bleeds of 6 seconds that stack, and nothing can block it because it comes from behind. It costs 20% of the cursed energy and only works when the enemy is within 100 pixels in front of him. If the enemy is farther away, forward + BLUE is the normal AIR CUT as before.
Nothing can touch Sukuna during the whole move. Afterwards he is standing behind the enemy, so the enemy is behind him.

Verity has another new BLUE move, LAG COUNTER. Walk back and tap BLUE: he plays his walking-backwards animation but does not move, and the picture stutters and jumps like a player with a bad connection. It lasts 1.5 seconds.

If the enemy hits him in that time, the hit does nothing to him. His top body is launched back (his legs stay where they are), then it snaps forward, bites the enemy, and he punches the enemy far away. The bite is his normal bite (12 damage and the bleeding) and the punch does 35 damage and knocks the enemy down. Nothing can touch him until it is over.

If nothing hits him in 1.5 seconds, the lag just ends and the energy is gone. It costs 15% of the cursed energy. In the SKILLS tree it is a new node under VERITY: LAG COUNTER, $400, and you need BITE first. The BLUE button says LAG when you hold back.
A blow that is not a fighter's swing (a curse, or a hit from behind) lands as usual and ends the lag. It is not in Wi-Fi fights yet.

Verity has a new BLUE move, RIP AND THROW. Walk forward and tap BLUE while the enemy is right in front of you: Verity's arms stretch out, he catches both of the enemy's hands and tries to rip him apart. It does not work, so he throws him back instead: 25 damage and the enemy is knocked down. While Verity holds him the enemy cannot move, and a guard does not help against it.
While Verity pulls, the enemy is stretched long and thin and shakes, then he snaps back just before the throw. The BLUE button says RIP (instead of BITE) when you are close enough to catch the enemy.
It costs 15% of the cursed energy. In the SKILLS tree it is a new node under VERITY: RIP AND THROW, $350, and you need BITE first.

If the enemy hits Verity while he is holding him, the enemy is let go.
